detail:
Cleveland Clinic notes that adenomyosis does not always cause symptoms, and that when symptoms such as heavy periods, cramping, or painful intercourse do occur, certain medications can help. Because the hormone estrogen promotes endometrial tissue growth, adenomyosis symptoms often go away after menopause. For pain, Cleveland Clinic describes nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, or NSAIDs, such as ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) or naproxen (Aleve), easing cramping.

Hormonal medications Cleveland Clinic describes include birth control pills, the Depo-Provera injection, and hormonal intrauterine devices (IUDs) such as Mirena, which can help with menstruation and abnormal bleeding. Surgery described includes adenomyomectomy, which removes adenomyosis from the uterine muscle, and hysterectomy: Cleveland Clinic notes that if a person does not plan to have children, a hysterectomy to remove the uterus can cure the condition.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about adenomyosis treatment options.
summary: Cleveland Clinic describes adenomyosis care as easing pain and heavy bleeding with anti-inflammatory pain medications and hormonal medications, with hysterectomy able to cure the condition, and symptoms tending to go away after menopause.
takeaways: nsaids such as ibuprofen or naproxen are described for cramping
hormonal options include pills, injections, and hormonal iuds
hysterectomy can cure adenomyosis; symptoms tend to ease after menopause
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Adenomyosis: easing pain and heavy bleeding
